spec.title: Tailscale2OTel — Exporter health
spec.description: tailscale2otel's own health, organised by pipeline stage: collection, ingestion, delivery, runtime, and cost/cardinality. Open this when a panel on tailscale2otel-tailnet is empty and you need to know whether the tailnet is quiet or the exporter is broken. Generated by deploy/grafana/gen/build.py.

spec.title: Exporter up
spec.description: Whether the process itself is reporting alive (tailscale2otel.up).

spec.title: Collectors OK
spec.description: Count of enabled collectors whose last scrape succeeded.

spec.title: Goroutines (summary)
spec.description: Current goroutine count — a runaway climb usually means a stuck collector or a leaking retry loop.

spec.title: GOMAXPROCS (summary)
spec.description: Go scheduler's configured max OS threads — mostly a deployment sanity check.

spec.title: Build info
spec.description: Running version / Go toolchain version (label values).

spec.title: Scrape success by collector (summary)
spec.description: 1/0 success flag per enabled collector's most recent scrape attempt.

spec.title: Last scrape age (summary)
spec.description: Seconds since each collector's last scrape — a row aging past its configured interval means that collector stopped running.

spec.title: API requests/s by status (summary)
spec.description: Tailscale API call volume by HTTP status — a rising non-2xx share is the exporter losing its ability to collect, before any collector shows it as down.

spec.title: Export outcome rate (summary)
spec.description: OTLP export attempts completed per second, by outcome (success/failure). Requires self_observability.enabled — absent otherwise.

spec.title: Export latency by signal (summary)
spec.description: OTLP export latency quantiles, by signal (metrics/logs/traces). Requires self_observability.enabled — absent otherwise.

spec.title: Config valid
spec.description: Whether the running config passed validation at startup.

spec.title: Config warnings
spec.description: Active configuration advisories from startup (a count, despite the _ratio suffix).

spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: Time since the process started.

spec.title: Checkpoint disk
spec.description: On-disk size of the file-backed checkpoint store.

defaults.noValue: No checkpoint file — the store is not file-backed, or nothing has persisted yet.

spec.title: Process CPU (summary)
spec.description: CPU seconds/s by mode (~cores).

spec.title: Checkpoint persist age
spec.description: Absent when the checkpoint store is not file-backed (in-memory).

defaults.noValue: No checkpoint file — the store is not file-backed, or nothing has persisted yet.

spec.title: Scrape errors/s
spec.description: Collector scrape attempts that failed, by collector.

spec.title: Checkpoint persist errors/s
spec.description: Checkpoint-store writes that failed, by collector.

spec.title: Component errors/s
spec.description: Internal component errors, by component.

spec.title: Admin auth rejected/s
spec.description: Admin-endpoint requests rejected by auth, by reason.

spec.title: API 429 / retries (summary)
spec.description: Rate-limit responses and the retries they trigger, fleet-wide.

spec.title: Node-metrics targets up
spec.description: Node-metrics scrape targets currently reachable.

spec.title: Node-metrics targets total
spec.description: Node-metrics scrape targets configured/discovered, up or down.

spec.title: Node-metrics discovery OK
spec.description: Whether the last node-metrics target-discovery pass succeeded.

spec.title: Node-metrics discovered targets
spec.description: Scrape targets found by the last node-metrics discovery pass.

spec.title: Node-metrics scrape health by target
spec.description: Per-target node-metrics scrape health (1=up).

spec.title: Scrape duration p50/p95/p99 by collector
spec.description: Per-collector scrape wall-clock duration quantiles from the histogram series.

spec.title: Last scrape duration by collector
spec.description: Wall-clock duration of each collector's most recent scrape (gauge, distinct from the p50/p95/p99 quantiles derived from the histogram series to its left).

spec.title: Scrape success by collector
spec.description: 1 when a collector's last scrape succeeded, 0 when it failed.

spec.title: Last scrape age
spec.description: Seconds since each collector's last scrape.

spec.title: Scrape errors/s by collector / type
spec.description: Collector scrape attempts that failed, by collector and error type.

spec.title: Scrape staleness
spec.description: Time since each collector's last successful scrape.

spec.title: Scrape budget headroom
spec.description: Last scrape duration as a fraction of the collector's poll interval; near or above 1 means the scrape risks overrunning its interval.

spec.title: API requests/s by status & endpoint
spec.description: Tailscale API requests issued per second, by HTTP status code and by endpoint (two independent group-bys over the same counter, on one axis).

spec.title: API retries/s by endpoint
spec.description: Tailscale API calls retried (429/5xx/timeout), by endpoint.

spec.title: API latency p50/p95/p99 by endpoint
spec.description: Per-endpoint Tailscale API latency quantiles.

spec.title: API 429 / retries
spec.description: Rate-limit responses and the retries they trigger, fleet-wide.

spec.title: Rate-limiter wait p50/p95/p99 by endpoint
spec.description: Time a request spent blocked on the client-side rate limiter (tailscale.http.rate_limit) before its first attempt.

spec.title: Time waiting vs time on the wire
spec.description: Seconds spent per second waiting on the client limiter versus actually on the wire to the Tailscale API.

spec.title: Requests delayed by the rate limiter
spec.description: Share of API requests that actually blocked on the client-side rate limiter.

spec.title: API operation last-probe age
spec.description: Seconds since each API operation was last probed; a row aging past its collector's interval means that operation stopped being exercised.

spec.title: Capability state by collector
spec.description: The current state of each enabled collector, filtered to the state that is set (disabled/scope_denied/ok).

defaults.noValue: No capability-preflight series. Requires self_observability.enabled; the scope preflight additionally requires tailscale.auth.method: oauth, as an API key carries no scope list to compare against.

spec.title: OAuth scope preflight by capability
spec.description: Advisory startup preflight comparing configured OAuth scopes against upstream's documented per-capability requirements.

defaults.noValue: No capability-preflight series. Requires self_observability.enabled; the scope preflight additionally requires tailscale.auth.method: oauth, as an API key carries no scope list to compare against.

spec.title: API operation availability by state
spec.description: Per-operation availability, the finer-grained sibling of the capability table above — which individual API operation is in a non-ok state.

defaults.noValue: No capability-preflight series. Requires self_observability.enabled; the scope preflight additionally requires tailscale.auth.method: oauth, as an API key carries no scope list to compare against.

spec.title: Pull-endpoint scrape duration p50/p95/p99 by outcome
spec.description: Wall-clock time serving one Prometheus /metrics request (gather + encode + write), by classified outcome — what the scraper's own timeout races against.

defaults.noValue: No Prometheus pull-endpoint series. Requires prometheus.enabled and at least one scrape against the exporter's /metrics endpoint.

spec.title: Pull-endpoint scrapes/s by outcome
spec.description: Prometheus /metrics scrapes served after the auth gate, by classified outcome (success/unavailable/error). A flat success rate is how a scraper that stopped asking is told apart from an endpoint that stopped answering.

defaults.noValue: No Prometheus pull-endpoint series. Requires prometheus.enabled and at least one scrape against the exporter's /metrics endpoint.

spec.title: Pull-endpoint requests in flight
spec.description: Prometheus /metrics requests currently being served. Pinned at prometheus.max_requests_in_flight means scrapes are being shed; a value that never returns to zero means collection is hanging rather than slow.

defaults.noValue: No Prometheus pull-endpoint series. Requires prometheus.enabled and at least one scrape against the exporter's /metrics endpoint.

spec.title: Pull-endpoint gather errors/s
spec.description: Prometheus registry Gather errors hit while serving /metrics; the handler continues on error and returns 200 with the remaining series, so a non-zero rate means series are silently being dropped from every scrape.

spec.title: Pull-endpoint auth rejections/s by reason
spec.description: Prometheus /metrics requests refused by the auth gate before being counted as a scrape, by reason (missing/bad credentials, or auth_required misconfiguration on a network-reachable bind).

defaults.noValue: No Prometheus pull-endpoint series. Requires prometheus.enabled and at least one scrape against the exporter's /metrics endpoint.

spec.title: Enrich cache age
spec.description: Age of the device-enrichment cache, which maps IPs and node IDs to device names for flow and audit records. It is populated by the devices collector: if that collector is disabled or failing this climbs, and enrichment silently degrades to unknown/external.

spec.title: Enrich cache size
spec.description: Devices held in the enrichment cache. A count well below the tailnet's device count means flow and audit records are resolving to unknown for the remainder.

spec.title: rDNS cache fill
spec.description: rDNS cache entries as a fraction of configured capacity.

spec.title: rDNS lookup hit-rate
spec.description: Share of rDNS lookups served from cache rather than an upstream query. 'of which stale' is the part served past its TTL while a refresh ran (enrichment.reverse_dns.stale_ttl) — those names are still correct, just older than cache_ttl.

spec.title: rDNS upstream queries/s
spec.description: Upstream PTR queries issued and cache evictions, per second. The refresh series are the subset of those queries triggered by a stale-serving hit.

spec.title: rDNS cache overflows vs lookups/s
spec.description: An overflow is a hot-path miss for a NEW address that could not be scheduled because the cache was already at enrichment.reverse_dns.max_entries — the address is simply never resolved. Read it against the accepted lookup rate: a sustained non-zero share means max_entries is too small.

defaults.noValue: No reverse-DNS cache series. Requires enrichment.reverse_dns.enabled and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Per-tailnet API errors
spec.description: Tailscale API 4xx/5xx responses per second, split out per tailnet on a multi-tailnet deployment.

spec.title: Object-store age (cursor & newest object)
spec.description: End-to-end ingestion lag (now minus the last cycle's persisted timestamp) beside how fresh the EXPORT's own writes are, independent of what was ingested. -1 on the second series means the cycle listed no object with a usable timestamp, deliberately distinguishable from a fresh zero-second age.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object-store gaps clear
spec.description: One when no unresolved gap remains; zero means at least one pending or quarantined object is outstanding.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object listing complete
spec.description: One means unexamined listing ground remains after the last cycle, which makes the backlog and oldest-pending-age panels lower bounds rather than totals.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Backlog & oldest pending object age
spec.description: Objects listed but not yet ingested, and how stale the next one to be processed already is. Zero here pairs with a zero backlog and means nothing is queued.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Unresolved gaps & oldest gap age
spec.description: FAILED objects awaiting retry or operator acknowledgement, and the age of the oldest. A gap aging without the count falling is an object failing repeatedly rather than recovering.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Objects & records ingested/s, bytes read vs decompressed
spec.description: Objects fully ingested and flow-log records decoded out of them (left axis, cps), beside transfer cost (compressed bytes actually read) against expansion (decompressed bytes consumed, right axis, Bps).

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object ingestion loss (skipped / retried / limit-stopped)
spec.description: Every reason an object or row was not ingested cleanly, on one axis: per-row skips (decode_error/semantic_invalid are single rows discarded from an otherwise-complete object; per_cycle_budget means the per-cycle object cap is holding ingestion behind the bucket), object-level retries (a failed object becomes a durable gap, retried under bounded backoff), and attempts stopped by a configured wire-byte/decompressed-byte/record-count budget.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Undecodable objects (broken feed)
spec.description: Whole objects that decoded ZERO records while at least one row failed — the signature of an export whose framing is not newline-delimited records. Treat any non-zero value as a feed-level fault, not corrupt data.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Object-store provider requests/s & latency
spec.description: TRANSPORT health only: `error` means the LIST or GET call itself returned an error, never a decode/validation/framing/limit failure (those are the ingestion-loss panel above). A body that fails mid-read counts as a SUCCESSFUL get here. Latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99, right axis in seconds) time the provider call itself — for `get` that is obtaining the object's reader, not streaming/decompressing/decoding its body.

defaults.noValue: No object-store ingestion series. Requires collectors.flowlogs.objectstore (or collectors.auditlogs.objectstore) with the matching source: objectstore, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Ingress WAL pending & retained entries
spec.description: Durable entries awaiting processor application and flush, staging files kept for bounded recovery cleanup, and transient completion markers awaiting durable cleanup. Pending climbing toward ingress_wal.max_entries fails new requests closed.

defaults.noValue: No ingress-WAL series. Requires ingress_wal.enabled together with a receiver that accepts payloads (streaming or webhook), and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Ingress WAL on-disk bytes
spec.description: Encoded bytes on the WAL filesystem. There is no TTL or eviction, so this is bounded only by ingress_wal.max_bytes.

defaults.noValue: No ingress-WAL series. Requires ingress_wal.enabled together with a receiver that accepts payloads (streaming or webhook), and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Subrequest attempts & failures/s
spec.description: Per-entity calls made inside a scrape (one posture-attributes call per device, and so on) — the N+1 cost a single scrape-duration figure hides — beside how many of them failed. A single entity's subrequest failing is non-fatal to the enclosing snapshot, so the collector still reports a clean scrape while coverage degrades; a scope_denied state is a missing OAuth scope, not a transient error.

defaults.noValue: No per-entity subrequest series. Requires a collector that fans out per entity — devices posture attributes, device invites, or user invites — and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Subrequest coverage (last pass)
spec.description: Fraction of per-entity subrequests that succeeded on the last pass. 1 when nothing was attempted: an empty tailnet has complete coverage of the entities it has.

defaults.noValue: No per-entity subrequest series. Requires a collector that fans out per entity — devices posture attributes, device invites, or user invites — and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Stream records/s by type
spec.description: Records accepted from the configured stream (HEC) receiver, by record type.

spec.title: Stream rejections & decode errors/s
spec.description: WHOLE requests refused before any record was extracted (rejected, by bounded reason) beside records extracted but that failed to decode into a known record type. Read against the accepted rate above.

spec.title: Webhook events by type & rejections by reason
spec.description: Webhook events accepted, by event type, beside deliveries rejected (bad signature, unknown event, etc.) by reason — accepted volume and its loss counter on one axis.

spec.title: Receiver in-flight & latency (stream)
spec.description: Requests currently being handled by the stream/webhook receivers (left axis) — a sustained non-zero value means the receiver is backed up. Stream (HEC) receiver request-handling latency quantiles ride the right axis (s); webhook has no equivalent latency histogram.

spec.title: Receiver rejected/s (stream + webhook)
spec.description: Requests rejected by either receiver, by reason — combines stream and webhook onto one axis.

spec.title: Stream records accepted vs skipped/s
spec.description: Skipped records were extracted from an otherwise-valid body and then never routed to a processor: `unclassified` matched neither the flow nor the audit shape, `unwrap_drop` was a non-object HEC event dropped while unwrapping. Read against the accepted rate.

defaults.noValue: No streaming-receiver series. Requires streaming.enabled with collectors.flowlogs.source or collectors.auditlogs.source set to stream.

spec.title: Webhook request duration p50/p95/p99
spec.description: Wall-clock handling time for webhook deliveries. Tailscale retries a delivery it considers timed out, so a rising tail here turns into duplicate events rather than lost ones.

defaults.noValue: No webhook-receiver series. Requires webhook.enabled and at least one Tailscale webhook endpoint delivering to it.

spec.title: Webhook accepted vs duplicates & schema drift/s
spec.description: Accepted volume alongside the redeliveries the dedup failsafe suppressed, and webhook payload schema observations by field. A field moving to an unknown status means Tailscale changed the payload shape: the receiver keeps accepting the event, so nothing else here goes red, but whatever the drifted field feeds is quietly no longer populated.

defaults.noValue: No webhook-receiver series. Requires webhook.enabled and at least one Tailscale webhook endpoint delivering to it.

spec.title: Ingest records/s & rejections/s & bytes/s by source
spec.description: Records accepted across every ingestion path, by source and signal, beside rejections and skips from every path on the same axis (left, cps). A source missing from the rejected series is a source that has never rejected anything, not one failing silently — the receivers are independently optional. Object-store contributes its skipped-object count, which includes per-cycle budget skips as well as faults. Decoded payload bytes accepted, by source, ride the right axis (Bps).

spec.title: Accepted event freshness & age p95, timestamp skew/s
spec.description: Seconds since the greatest event timestamp accepted from each source/signal (exposes stale-but-still-running ingestion, unlike receiver liveness alone); the p95 age at acceptance (backfills and retries raise this without moving the last-event timestamp backwards); and p95 upstream capture/observation delay where the wire format supplies a capture timestamp separately from event time. Right axis (cps): events whose timestamp is later than local acceptance, or whose capture timestamp precedes event time — negative derived durations are clamped to zero.

spec.title: Dedup hits & evictions/s
spec.description: Duplicate records suppressed by the cross-source dedup failsafe, per set, beside evictions from capacity pressure. Steady-state evictions are normal: dedup keys are effectively unique, so a full set evicts one key per insert forever even when healthy — only evictions approaching a set's capacity within one poll interval indicate real overlap loss.

spec.title: Dedup set fill
spec.description: Keys currently held in each bounded dedup set (a count, despite the metric's _ratio suffix).

spec.title: Processor queue fill by signal
spec.description: This app's own log/trace batch-processor queue (buffered between acceptance and OTLP export), current size as a fraction of its configured capacity, by signal. Near or at 1 means the queue is saturated and new records will start being dropped rather than buffered.

defaults.noValue: No processor-queue series. Requires self_observability.enabled and at least one log or trace export path active (the queue only exists once something is being batched for OTLP export).

spec.title: Processor queue drops/s by signal & reason
spec.description: Records/spans dropped because the queue above was full when offered, by signal and reason. Any non-zero rate means the fill fraction beside it was already at or near 1 — read the two together, the drop counter is the loss the fill gauge warned about.

spec.title: Log records & bytes truncated/s by field
spec.description: Log records whose body or an attribute value was truncated to a bounded length before export, by field (left axis, cps). Non-zero is expected on a very verbose source; a sustained climb on a field that was previously flat means an upstream payload shape got bigger, not that the exporter regressed. Bytes dropped by truncation, same field breakdown, right axis (Bps) — read together: a rising record count with flat bytes means many small truncations; flat count with rising bytes means the same records are losing more each time.

spec.title: Audit poll collector
spec.description:
Last poll-path scrape result for the auditlogs collector.

Reading this row — four states that otherwise look identical:

- **idle tailnet**: the collector scrape reads 1, the accepted counter has series, and both range counters read 0. Nothing happened.
- **absent Loki data**: the metric counter moved over this range but the Loki counter is 0. Events were accepted; the log records are not in the queried Loki datasource.
- **ingestion failure**: the scrape gauge reads 0, or the failures panel is non-zero. Records are being attempted and lost.
- **audit collection not enabled**: no scrape series and no accepted counter at all. This one is a floor, not a verdict — presence **cannot** separate a disabled collector from a provider that does not support the API from a process that was never deployed, so the empty states name the prerequisite instead of guessing why.

defaults.noValue: No auditlogs scrape reported. Prerequisites: collectors.auditlogs.enabled with collectors.auditlogs.source of poll or both. A stream, webhook or objectstore path reports no scrape here — read the ingestion-path panel. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Audit events accepted (this range)
spec.description:
Audit events the exporter accepted over the dashboard time range, from every ingestion path. Reads exactly $__range, the same window as its Loki counterpart — the two disagreeing on window is the classic false "the data is missing" report.

Reading this row — four states that otherwise look identical:

- **idle tailnet**: the collector scrape reads 1, the accepted counter has series, and both range counters read 0. Nothing happened.
- **absent Loki data**: the metric counter moved over this range but the Loki counter is 0. Events were accepted; the log records are not in the queried Loki datasource.
- **ingestion failure**: the scrape gauge reads 0, or the failures panel is non-zero. Records are being attempted and lost.
- **audit collection not enabled**: no scrape series and no accepted counter at all. This one is a floor, not a verdict — presence **cannot** separate a disabled collector from a provider that does not support the API from a process that was never deployed, so the empty states name the prerequisite instead of guessing why.

spec.title: Audit log lines in Loki (this range)
spec.description:
Audit log records present in the queried Loki datasource over the same $__range window. Materially below the accepted counter means the records were accepted but did not land where this dashboard reads them.

Reading this row — four states that otherwise look identical:

- **idle tailnet**: the collector scrape reads 1, the accepted counter has series, and both range counters read 0. Nothing happened.
- **absent Loki data**: the metric counter moved over this range but the Loki counter is 0. Events were accepted; the log records are not in the queried Loki datasource.
- **ingestion failure**: the scrape gauge reads 0, or the failures panel is non-zero. Records are being attempted and lost.
- **audit collection not enabled**: no scrape series and no accepted counter at all. This one is a floor, not a verdict — presence **cannot** separate a disabled collector from a provider that does not support the API from a process that was never deployed, so the empty states name the prerequisite instead of guessing why.

spec.title: Audit ingestion failures/s
spec.description:
Records the pipeline attempted and lost, by path. Any non-zero series here rules out the idle reading: something arrived and did not make it through.

Reading this row — four states that otherwise look identical:

- **idle tailnet**: the collector scrape reads 1, the accepted counter has series, and both range counters read 0. Nothing happened.
- **absent Loki data**: the metric counter moved over this range but the Loki counter is 0. Events were accepted; the log records are not in the queried Loki datasource.
- **ingestion failure**: the scrape gauge reads 0, or the failures panel is non-zero. Records are being attempted and lost.
- **audit collection not enabled**: no scrape series and no accepted counter at all. This one is a floor, not a verdict — presence **cannot** separate a disabled collector from a provider that does not support the API from a process that was never deployed, so the empty states name the prerequisite instead of guessing why.

spec.title: Tailscale deferred delay (p50/p95/p99)
spec.description: Time Tailscale deferred a configuration-audit record before logging it. Emitted only when the record carries both eventTime and deferredAt in order, so a quiet panel is not the same as a zero delay.

spec.title: Local processing delay (p50/p95/p99)
spec.description: Time from the record's deferredAt (or eventTime when it was not deferred) to local processor acceptance. Rising here with a flat deferred delay points at the poll window or the exporter, not at upstream.

spec.title: Audit schema drift
spec.description: Bounded known/unknown observations for audit action, origin, actor type, and target property. Raw unknown values never enter metric labels.

spec.title: Annotations published/s by category
spec.description: Grafana annotations accepted by the annotations API since process start, by category. Only emitted when grafana_annotations.url is set.

defaults.noValue: No Grafana annotation activity. Requires grafana_annotations.url to be configured.

spec.title: Annotations dropped/s by reason
spec.description: Annotations that did not reach Grafana, by bounded reason. `duplicate` is the steady state on a snapshot-shaped source (a key re-observed every poll while still inside its expiry window) and is not a fault; `queue_full` and `local_rate_limited` are this process's own guards; `unauthorized`, `rate_limited`, `rejected`, `server_error` and `transport` are Grafana's verdict — a climbing `unauthorized` is an expired or under-scoped token.

spec.title: Annotation delivery degraded
spec.description: Whether the most recent Grafana annotation write failed and has not yet been recovered by a later success. The counterpart to the dropped counter: that one says how much was lost, this says whether it is still happening.

defaults.noValue: No Grafana annotation activity. Requires grafana_annotations.url to be configured.

spec.title: Export latency p50/p95/p99 by signal
spec.description: OTLP export latency quantiles, by signal (metrics/logs/traces).

spec.title: Export outcome rate
spec.description: OTLP export attempts completed per second, by outcome (success/failure).

spec.title: Export failures/s by type
spec.description: OTLP export attempts that failed, by error type.

spec.title: Export spans/s
spec.description: Spans handed to the OTLP trace exporter — the trace cost proxy. Counts every span per export batch; empty when tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: Export diagnostics suppressed/s
spec.description: Export-failure diagnostic log lines suppressed during a sustained OTLP outage, by signal and error class. Exact — never itself rate-limited, so this is the true count of failures happening beneath the log-rate-limit floor.

spec.title: PII filter status
spec.description: Compliance view: every category should read 'emitted' (==1) unless redacted.

spec.title: Streams configured
spec.description: Configuration/network log streams delivering to a SIEM sink.

spec.title: Last delivery error
spec.description: 1 if any stream's last delivery reported an error (see the Delivery errors log).

defaults.noValue: No delivery status — no configured log stream has reported one.

spec.title: Delivery throughput by type
spec.description: Bytes sent to the configured SIEM sink, by log type.

spec.title: Entries delivered/s by type
spec.description: Log entries successfully delivered to the SIEM sink, by log type.

spec.title: Delivery requests/s by type
spec.description: Delivery requests attempted to the sink, per log type. Zero here with a configured stream means nothing is being sent at all, which the failure rate alone cannot show.

spec.title: Delivery failure ratio by type
spec.description: Failed share of attempted delivery requests. The denominator is clamped, so a type with no attempts reads 0 rather than dividing by zero.

spec.title: Failed requests/s by type
spec.description: Failed delivery requests to the sink — alert on a sustained rate.

spec.title: Backpressure: spoofed & max-body/s
spec.description: Entries rejected as spoofed and requests that hit the max body size (SIEM backpressure).

spec.title: Last activity age by type
spec.description: Time since the most recent delivery activity per log type (alert on staleness).

spec.title: Delivery errors
spec.description: Per-stream delivery errors; the error text is the log body.

spec.title: Scrape → API trace waterfall
spec.description: Trace panels are empty if tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: API p95 by endpoint (traces)
spec.description: Trace panels are empty if tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: Scrape cadence by collector (traces)
spec.description: Trace panels are empty if tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: stream.receive batch size (traces)
spec.description: Trace panels are empty if tracing.enabled=false.

spec.title: Goroutines
spec.description: Number of live goroutines (a count, despite the _ratio suffix).

spec.title: GOMAXPROCS
spec.description: Current GOMAXPROCS, the max OS threads executing Go code (a count, despite the _ratio suffix).

spec.title: Process uptime
spec.description: Seconds since the process started (wall-clock uptime).

spec.title: Process CPU (user/system)
spec.description: Cumulative process CPU time (getrusage RUSAGE_SELF), by mode, as a rate (~cores). Emitted on unix platforms only.

spec.title: Memory breakdown
spec.description: Go memory obtained from the OS (runtime.memory.sys), stacked into in-use heap, idle/reserved heap, stacks, and other non-heap runtime (GC, mspan/mcache). Total height = total sys.

spec.title: Goroutines & stack
spec.description: Goroutine count alongside stack memory, over time (the stat panel above shows only the current value).

spec.title: GC cycles/s
spec.description: Completed garbage-collection cycles per second.

spec.title: GC pause/s
spec.description: Cumulative stop-the-world GC pause time, as seconds of pause per second of wall clock.

spec.title: GC CPU fraction
spec.description: Fraction of total CPU time used by the garbage collector since process start (0..1).

spec.title: GC next-target vs live heap
spec.description: Live heap vs the heap size that triggers the next GC; the gap is GC headroom.

spec.title: Heap alloc churn
spec.description: Cumulative heap-allocation rate (includes freed); allocation churn / GC pressure.

spec.title: Live heap objects
spec.description: Number of live heap objects (a count, despite the _ratio suffix).

spec.title: Profile upload duration p50/p95/p99
spec.description: Wall-clock seconds per profile upload attempt, including failed ones. Rising latency here is the early warning for the upload timeout that follows.

defaults.noValue: No profile-upload series. Requires profiling.pyroscope.server_address to be set (the opt-in Pyroscope push agent).

spec.title: Profile upload attempts/s
spec.description: Profile upload attempts to Pyroscope, successful or not (one per profile type per profiling.pyroscope.upload_rate period). A flat line with the agent enabled means it is not uploading at all — a different fault from uploads being rejected.

defaults.noValue: No profile-upload series. Requires profiling.pyroscope.server_address to be set (the opt-in Pyroscope push agent).

spec.title: Profile upload failures/s by type
spec.description: Profile upload attempts that failed, by bounded error type (timeout, canceled, unauthenticated, rate_limited, unavailable, tls, invalid, other) — never the server's response body.

defaults.noValue: No profile-upload series. Requires profiling.pyroscope.server_address to be set (the opt-in Pyroscope push agent).

spec.title: Profile upload consecutive failures
spec.description: Current unbroken profile-upload failure streak, reset to 0 by any success (a count, despite the _ratio suffix). Distinguishes a blip from a sustained outage without needing a rate window.

defaults.noValue: No profile-upload series. Requires profiling.pyroscope.server_address to be set (the opt-in Pyroscope push agent).

spec.title: Profile upload last-success age
spec.description: Seconds since the most recent SUCCESSFUL profile upload; absent until the first success (last_success is 0 until then, filtered out rather than charted as a huge age). The attempts counter keeps climbing during an outage, so this is what actually catches profiles silently stopping.

defaults.noValue: No profile-upload series. Requires profiling.pyroscope.server_address to be set (the opt-in Pyroscope push agent).

spec.title: TLS certificate expiry countdown
spec.description: Seconds until the active certificate's notAfter (expiry), by listener component (admin|metrics|stream). Falling toward zero is what 'TLS certificate expiring' pages on.

defaults.noValue: No TLS certificate series. Requires TLS to be configured on at least one listener (admin, metrics, or stream).

spec.title: TLS certificate reload failures
spec.description: Certificate reload attempts that failed to produce a valid keypair, by listener component. The listener keeps serving the last known-good certificate; a non-zero rate is a rotation going wrong, and is what 'TLS certificate reload failing' pages on.

defaults.noValue: No TLS certificate series. Requires TLS to be configured on at least one listener (admin, metrics, or stream).

spec.title: TLS certificate age since issuance
spec.description: Seconds since the active certificate's notBefore, by listener component. Updates on every successful reload, so a value that stops growing at a reload boundary and then jumps means a rotation landed.

defaults.noValue: No TLS certificate series. Requires TLS to be configured on at least one listener (admin, metrics, or stream).

spec.title: TLS certificate reload freshness
spec.description: Seconds since the most recent successful certificate reload, by listener component; absent until the first success. A rotated file on disk is picked up on the next handshake at least this recently.

defaults.noValue: No TLS certificate series. Requires TLS to be configured on at least one listener (admin, metrics, or stream).

spec.title: Metrics over cardinality cap
spec.description: Metric families that exceeded the per-metric series cap (cardinality.metric_limit, default 10000) and are now collapsing excess series into one otel_metric_overflow series — SILENT per-series detail loss. >0 means raise metric_limit or lower flow cardinality (ephemeral source_port is the biggest driver).

spec.title: Busiest metric — % of cap
spec.description: Highest per-metric active-series count as a fraction of the 10k cap.

spec.title: Total active series
spec.description: Sum of active series across all tailscale2otel metrics (a proxy for ingest cost).

spec.title: Metric families tracked
spec.description: Distinct tailscale2otel metric families currently reporting an active-series count.

spec.title: Overflowing families
spec.description: Metric families currently over the per-metric cap (otel_metric_overflow=true).

defaults.noValue: No metrics over cap — all series fully resolved.

spec.title: Active series vs 10k cap (top $topn)
spec.description: Per-metric active series against the cap. Watch the flow families.

spec.title: Active series over time (top $topn)
spec.description: Per-metric active series (cap 10k) over time, top-N by current value. Watch the flow families.

spec.title: Flow series: raw vs bounded rollup
spec.description: Raw flow families saturate the 10k cap; the bounded rollup stays small. When raw is at cap, trust the ROLLUP talker panels on the Network tab.

spec.title: __other__ rollup share
spec.description: Fraction of rollup bytes folded into the bounded __other__ bucket. High = many small talkers.

spec.title: Flow log records dropped/s
spec.description: Flow LOG records suppressed by the per-window volume guard (collectors.flowlogs.max_log_records_per_window). Metrics are never dropped, only logs.

spec.title: Dedup set size
spec.description: Keys held in each cross-source de-duplication set (a count).

spec.title: Dedup evictions/s
spec.description: Steady-state evictions are normal: dedup keys are effectively unique, so a full set evicts one key per insert forever even when healthy. Only evictions approaching a set's capacity within one poll interval indicate real overlap loss (boundary double-counting).

spec.title: Series limit
spec.description: Configured per-metric series limit (cardinality.metric_limit). 0 means unlimited.

defaults.noValue: No per-metric series cap reported — needs cardinality.metric_limit set (unset means unlimited) and exporter self-observability.

spec.title: Overflowing now
spec.description: Number of metric families currently overflowing their series cap. >0 means detail loss.

spec.title: Per-metric headroom (top-N)
spec.description: Per-metric active-series count divided by the series limit — headroom as a fraction. 1.0 = at cap. Uses / on() group_left() because the limit is a single unlabelled series.

spec.expr: topk($topn, max by (metric_name) (tailscale2otel_series_active) / on() group_left() max(tailscale2otel_series_limit))

spec.title: Active series by group
spec.description: Active series aggregated by metric_group — the primary cost-driver view. 18 groups live; each group maps to a logical collector domain.

spec.title: Metrics overflowing now
spec.description: Metric families where overflowing_ratio == 1 (capped). 147+ series tracked; 0 overflowing is the normal live state — that is correct.

defaults.noValue: No metrics overflowing.

spec.title: Ingest vs export cost (per minute)
spec.description: Export datapoints/min and log records/min (ingest cost) alongside per-source ingest rate. Rising DPM driven by a single source → check that group in 'Active series by group'.

spec.title: Forwarded metric-name drops/s by reason
spec.description: Samples dropped because their metric NAME had not been seen before and the distinct-name budget (node_metrics.max_distinct_metrics, default 2000) was already exhausted. Targets choose their own names and each new one creates a permanent instrument, so the budget is a hard bound on a node-controlled input. Read the drop rate against the active uncataloged series count on the right axis: that is the population the budget governs. Sustained drops mean raising max_distinct_metrics or tightening metric_allow/metric_deny.

defaults.noValue: No node-metrics name-budget series. Requires node_metrics.enabled with at least one target, and self_observability.enabled.

spec.title: Metric names dropped over the window
spec.description: Total forwarded samples lost to the distinct-name budget over the dashboard's time range. Any non-zero value means a scrape target is presenting more distinct metric names than the budget allows.

defaults.noValue: No node-metrics name-budget series. Requires node_metrics.enabled with at least one target, and self_observability.enabled.
